messages:
lina: Heads up — we should build a small Grafana dashboard that surfaces 'thermal drift' across GPUs (inlet vs ambient delta over time). Current SRE runbook only checks absolute temps and power, but not sustained inlet delta, which is what predicts cooling regressions.
omar: love this. can we keep it lightweight? a couple of panels + an alert for sustained drift.
janet: what queries do you have in mind?
lina: thinking panels: 1) per-gpu 95th percentile inlet-ambient delta (24h), 2) rack-level avg delta with tenant overlays, 3) power vs delta scatter (last 1h), 4) annotation lane for thermostat setpoint changes / maintenance windows.
timo: for tenant overlays — do we have labels on metrics for tenant_id or allocation_id? otherwise per-rack is easiest.
janet: alloc labels exist on nvml exporter metrics (allocation, region). we can join via node labels for rack/zone.
ops-bot: reminder: grafana provisioning is managed in repo infra/grafana/dashboards — PRs must include UID and JSON schema v2.
lina: here's a starting PromQL for per-gpu inlet delta (feel free to tweak):
```
quantile_over_time(0.95, (nvml_gpu_inlet_temp_celsius - node_ambient_temp_celsius)[24h:5m])
```
omar: hmm, ambient metric is node-level while nvml is device-level. we should use a per-device ambient approximation: avg by (instance) (node_ambient_temp_celsius) and then join with gpu metric by instance. e.g. using label_replace or on(instance).
janet: also consider recording rule to precompute gpu:inlet_delta:95p per 5m window so dashboards and alerting are cheap. e.g. in prometheus-rules: gpu:inlet_delta:95p = quantile_over_time(0.95, (nvml_gpu_inlet_temp_celsius - node_ambient_temp_celsius)[1h:5m])
timo: alert proposal: Alert if gpu:inlet_delta:95p > 7 for 10m AND region != "test". spike alert if delta > 12 for 5m. both should attach top-20 GPUs by delta.
lina: agree on thresholds. let's also gate alerts behind low CPU/noisy-neighbor exclusions — sometimes thermal delta jumps during batch runs and is expected. add label `workload_type=throughput` to mute if present.
omar: panel tips — use timeseries with lines+points, and a table panel with top offenders (delta, power, allocation). grafana transform to pivot by allocation and show sparkline.
janet: for power correlation scatter: x=delta 95p, y=nvml_gpu_power_watts avg over 5m, color by allocation. we can compute via PromQL vector matching.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: grafana provisioning lint passed for test dashboards (automated).
lina: I'll sketch a dashboard JSON and open a PR to infra/grafana/dashboards/gpu-thermal-drift.json by EOD. can one of you review the recording rule in prometheus-rules?
timo: I can review. please include example alerts with runbook links.
omar: include an explanation snippet in the dashboard description: what 'thermal drift' means, why it matters (fan control hysteresis, future cooling failure), and recommended mitigations (balancing, firmware, rack cfm checks).
janet: small UX ask — add a region selector dropdown (region label) at top + a time-range preset for 'last 6h' and '24h 95p'.
lina: noted. Also want an annotation stream from ops that marks cooldown windows and AC maintenance. ops-bot can we push AC events to grafana annotations?
ops-bot: yes — ops-bot will post annotations when a maintenance ticket is created with `ops/maintenance` tag. include ticket id in annotation text.
omar: sounds good. once PR is up i'll run load tests to ensure panel queries don't spike prometheus. if heavy, we'll rely on recording rules.
lina: perfect. thanks y'all. I'll ping the PR link here when ready :thumbsup:
ops-bot: ticket created: MAINT-4627 (AC inspection scheduled) — annotation will appear on dashboard when PR merges.
janet: quick followup: add a discrete panel showing % of GPUs with delta > 7 (1h window) — great for high-level SLO.
lina: good call. add it to the top row. I'll include SLO note: 'SLO target: <5% GPUs with delta>7 over rolling 1h' in dashboard description.
marc: (brief) can we also tag devices with hardware generation so we can filter older cards?
janet: yes, exporter already exposes `gpu_model` label. include as filter.
lina: thanks — i'll incorporate filters: region, rack, gpu_model, allocation. PR incoming.
